name: black-hat-offense

findings.title: validateHandlerOrder bypasses max-only pricing bounds when computeRatioX96 overflows to 0
findings.description: In AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder (lines 198-226), when computeRatioX96 returns 0 due to overflow (extreme amountOut/amountIn ratio), the max price bound check at line 221 evaluates as: maxSqrtPriceX96 != 0 && 0 > maxSqrtPriceX96, which is always false. A CLOB order with an astronomically high price passes validation despite max-only pricing bounds being set. In contrast, _validatePricingBounds (line 847) explicitly reverts on sqrtPriceX96 == 0, but validateHandlerOrder lacks this check.
findings.impact: Token creators who set only a maximum price ceiling (common pattern for preventing price spikes) get no protection against handler orders with overflow-level prices. CLOB makers can place extreme price orders that bypass intended bounds, enabling price manipulation on CLOB orderbooks.
findings.proof_sketch: Forge test: test_HR02_overflowPriceBypasses_maxOnlyBounds in AuditStateDesyncKnowledgeLoop.t.sol. Set max-only bounds (min=0, max=1e30), call validateHandlerOrder with amountIn=1, amountOut=type(uint256).max. computeRatioX96 returns 0 (overflow). Max check fails to catch it. No revert. Halmos symbolic execution also confirms: 1 path, 0 failures.
findings.victim: Token creators relying on max-only pricing bounds to protect their token market
findings.extractable_value: Depends on CLOB order book depth and token liquidity
attack_sequence: 1. Token creator sets max-only pricing bounds via registry (min=0, max=X)
2. Attacker places CLOB order with amountIn=1, amountOut=type(uint256).max
3. computeRatioX96 overflows, returns 0
4. validateHandlerOrder: maxCheck = (X != 0 && 0 > X) = false. Order accepted.
5. Order with infinite effective price bypasses creator's intended ceiling
prerequisites: Token with AMMStandardHook as token hook
CLOB handler for the token pair

findings.title: Whitelist ID change via registryUpdateTokenSettings leaves hook with empty whitelist, blocking direct swaps
confidence_deductions: Impact is DoS not fund extraction (-15)
Admin can fix by syncing whitelist content (-5)
findings.description: When setTokenSettings changes pairedTokenWhitelistId from 1 to 2 and syncs to hook, only _tokenSettings is updated via registryUpdateTokenSettings. The hook's _pairTokenWhitelists[2] remains empty because whitelist CONTENT is synced separately. For direct swaps (poolId==0), _validateTokenTradingRules checks _pairTokenWhitelists[newId].contains(pairedToken), which fails for all tokens. This creates asymmetric DoS: direct swaps break while pool swaps continue unaffected.
findings.impact: All direct swaps for the token fail until admin separately syncs whitelist 2 content to hook
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Token has whitelist 1 with WETH, synced to hook. 2. Admin changes to whitelist 2 via setTokenSettings(hooksToSync=[hook]). 3. Hook has pairedTokenWhitelistId=2 but _pairTokenWhitelists[2] is empty. 4. Direct swap with WETH reverts PairNotAllowed.
findings.victim: Direct swap users of the affected token
attack_sequence: Admin syncs whitelist 1 content and settings to hook
Admin changes settings to reference whitelist 2 and syncs settings to hook
Admin forgets to separately sync whitelist 2 content
All direct swaps fail with PairNotAllowed
prerequisites: Admin changes whitelist ID without syncing new whitelist content
code_smells: AMMStandardHook.sol:522 - settings update doesn't trigger whitelist content sync
findings.what_remains_unverified: Whether this is considered by-design (documented desync model)

findings.title: CLOB calculateFixedInput double rounding causes cumulative overconsumption in multi-order fills
confidence_deductions: Griefing vector only - attacker does not profit (-20)
Requires many small orders at specific price points (-15)
DoS is limited to specific order book, not protocol-wide (-10)
findings.description: calculateFixedInput (CLOBHelper.sol:309-315) applies mulDivRoundingUp twice. When filling N small orders, cumulative output exceeds single-shot calculation by up to 2*N wei. AMM provides single-shot output but CLOB consumes cumulative output, reverting with InsufficientOutputToFill.
findings.impact: Griefing: attacker places many minimum-size orders, causing legitimate fills to revert. Attacker loses gas and deposit cost. No value extraction.
findings.proof_sketch: Forge test confirmed: single-shot output for input=300 at price=Q96+1 is 302. Sum of 100 fills of input=3 each is 500. Difference of 198 wei (66% overconsumption). Fill would revert with InsufficientOutputToFill.
findings.victim: Takers attempting to fill orders (DoS, not extraction)
attack_sequence: 1. Attacker places 100+ minimum-size orders at a price where rounding compounds
2. Legitimate taker submits swap to fill the order book
3. AMM computes amountOut using single-shot calculation (302 wei)
4. CLOB fills orders individually, each rounding up (cumulative 500 wei)
5. Fill reverts with InsufficientOutputToFill (500 > 302)
6. Attacker closes orders and withdraws deposit
prerequisites: Many small orders at specific price where rounding compounds
code_smells: CLOBHelper.sol:313-314 - double mulDivRoundingUp causes cumulative rounding divergence from single-shot
findings.what_remains_unverified: Whether this is exploitable in practice with real token amounts (test used small values). The rounding difference may be negligible with 18-decimal tokens.
